messages:
elena_support: FYI - customer says their support bot answers got noticeably more direct and shorter after the model bump yesterday. They filed a ticket and included before/after examples. Asking for triage. :eyes:

deploy-bot: rolled out redwood-serve-v4.2.0 to hosted cluster us-west-2 at 1994999000 (canary -> 100%).

jamie_engineer: Can you paste the customer's curl and the example prompts/responses? We should confirm it's the model change and not a prompt concat issue.

elena_support: Pasting excerpts from the support ticket (customer redacted):

Customer prompt: "How do I reset my password for an account I no longer have access to?"

Response (prior model v4.1.x):
"You can reset your password by following these steps: 1) Go to Settings > Account; 2) Click 'Forgot password' and enter your email; 3) Follow the password reset email link. If you don't have access to that email, contact support with proof of identity and we'll assist you. Would you like me to draft an email template for that?"

Response (after v4.2.0 rollout):
"Use Settings > Account -> 'Forgot password', enter your email, follow the reset email. If you can't access the email, contact support with proof of identity."

Notes: customer says the newer reply drops the offer-to-help and some hedging language. They report this happening across multiple intents (billing, billing disputes, onboarding). Token difference for that example: before 48 tokens, after 29 tokens.

rachel_ml: Interesting. That's a subtle brevity / reduced scaffolding change, not a factual error. Could be due to calibration tweak in the prompt system or a change in default temperature/penalty or a new safety/conciseness policy baked into the model version. Any chance their SDK is setting max_tokens or stop tokens?

elena_support: Customer included their API call (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' 
 -d '{"model":"redwood-serve","model_version":"v4.2.0","input":"How do I reset my password for an account I no longer have access to?","max_tokens":150,"temperature":0.2}'
```

jamie_engineer: They explicitly pass model_version v4.2.0. Can we pull the rollout notes to see what changed between v4.1.x and v4.2.0? @rachel_ml any known instruction-following regresses?

rachel_ml: I pulled the changelog: main differences were improved token efficiency and a new brevity loss added during instruction fine-tuning to reduce verbosity on short queries. That could trim scaffolding. We also applied a tiny decrease to top_p and a post-processing cutoff to prefer shorter completions under certain prompts.

sam_platform: config snippet from rollout pipeline (from infra):
```
model: redwood-serve
version: v4.2.0
policy: {
  brevity_bias: 0.12,
  instruction_loss_weight_adjust: -0.03
}
```

jamie_engineer: OK that matches customer experience. Two quick asks: 1) can we reproduce with an internal A/B (v4.1.9 vs v4.2.0) using the exact payload? 2) if reproduced, propose a mitigation (revert brevity_bias, or add a per-customer prompt prefix override).

elena_support: Customer is asking for a rollback or a knob they can set to preserve prior verbosity. They noted the change impacts tone in transactional replies and reduces perceived helpfulness.

rachel_ml: I'll spin up a quick repro harness. Prefer to run both models with same decoding params and see length distributions over a small prompt set (password reset, billing refund, onboarding steps).

ops-bot: provisioning instance p-qa-ml-03 (v4.1.9) and p-qa-ml-04 (v4.2.0) - ready in ~4m.

jamie_engineer: If we confirm brevity_bias is the cause, short-term mitigation: add a new system prompt template tier that injects a micro-polite scaffold: e.g., prepend "Offer an optional follow-up question and an offer to assist". We can expose that as a per-customer setting in the console while we tune the global loss.

elena_support: I'll update the customer with ETA and ask whether they prefer immediate rollback for their workspace or a per-workspace verbosity setting.

rachel_ml: Quick preliminary result: for the password reset prompt, v4.1.9 median tokens=52, v4.2.0 median tokens=30, and fractional inclusion of "Would you like me to..." dropped from 62% -> 8%. Repro confirmed.

jamie_engineer: Thanks. Action items: @rachel_ml open an RFC describing the brevity_loss impact + rollback criteria. @sam_platform add a console toggle for 'preserve verbosity' scoped to workspaces (short-term feature flag). @elena_support coordinate rollback request if customer wants it. I'll prepare a short customer-facing statement if we do rollback.

elena_support: sounds good. Customer preferred a per-workspace toggle first. Marking P1-Escalation. I'll attach the ticket ID in the support system. :white_check_mark:

jamie_engineer: tagging this for postmortem if we don't catch similar regressions in evals. :thinking:

rachel_ml: Also adding a small prompt-set to our regression harness to catch scaffold-elisions (password reset, cancellation flows, refunds).

elena_support: Thanks team. I'll post updates here after customer confirmation and when the flag is live.
